title: Structured spawn identity — finding_signature hash, not free-form spawn_finding_id
body: F001's spawn metadata carries five fields — parent_audit_id, finding_id, finding_code, finding_class, finding_signature — instead of a single free-form `spawn_finding_id`. `finding_signature` is a deterministic SHA-256 hex prefix of `{finding_code}|{finding_class}|{normalized_issue}` where normalized_issue is whitespace-collapsed lowercase issue text. The repeated-finding hard stop in `check_repeated_finding` compares signatures, NOT just `(code, class)` pairs — `(EC5, correctness)` is too broad to gate on alone (a single auditor can produce dozens of distinct EC5 correctness findings across plans without any of them being 'the same finding'). Why: (a) auditor outputs cluster around a small set of codes/classes but each instance has different concrete issue text; the signature distinguishes 'auditor flagged the same problem twice across nested plans' from 'auditor flagged two different problems that share a code'; (b) signature collision is what we actually want to hard-stop — a repeated SAME finding climbing the parent chain is the inception-loss shape; (c) `audit_id#finding-N` strings are too unstable across re-runs (audit_id includes iteration counter). How to apply: any future severity classifier or duplicate-finding detector should use `finding_signature` as the identity key, not `(code, class)` or `audit_id#finding-N`. The signature also surfaces drift evidence — if the auditor changes the issue text after the spawn-finding was recorded, the signature recomputed at parse time will mismatch the declared signature, and Pydantic validation rejects the parse with 'declared signature does not match recomputed signature' (auditor changed the finding underneath us; operator must re-author the spawn metadata).

title: --allow-depth N is CLI-only; frontmatter cannot raise the platform cap
body: F001's `--allow-depth N` is the ONLY mechanism for dispatching above the platform default depth_limit of 3. plan.md frontmatter MAY declare a LOWER `orchestration.depth_limit` (a per-plan tightening), but cannot raise it; values > 3 are rejected at Pydantic-validation time. Why: (a) intent is to keep depth expansion as a per-dispatch operator decision, not a per-plan default — frontmatter overrides invite scope-creep depth bumps that compound across the plan tree; (b) CLI flag is more friction (operator types it explicitly each time, has to think about why), which is the correct friction for a sensitive override; (c) the override is recorded in `validation_performed` of the audit envelope as `depth_override applied (N)` so the audit trail surfaces every time the cap was lifted. How to apply: any future per-dispatch override (e.g., quota cap, breaker bypass) should follow this CLI-only pattern unless there's a strong argument for plan-level configurability. Frontmatter is for plan-stable configuration; CLI is for operator-instant decisions.

title: commit_policy.mode defaults to evidence_only; code-writing authority must be explicit
body: F002's `commit_policy.mode` defaults to `evidence_only`. Implementation children that need to commit code must explicitly declare BOTH `mode: child_commit` AND `child_charter.may_edit_product_code: true`; the cross-field invariant is enforced at Pydantic validation time. The `may_edit_product_code` field has NO default — it must be set explicitly. Why: (a) safe-by-default — a child plan that fails to declare its commit intent should NOT silently inherit code-writing authority; the most conservative default ('I can produce evidence under evidence/ but I will not commit code') is the right starting point; (b) makes intent visible in the plan.md frontmatter so the operator's pre-impl review surfaces 'is this child supposed to be writing code?' as a foreground question, not a buried default; (c) prevents a class of accidents where a child plan was authored quickly without a commit_policy block and then proceeded to commit changes that bypassed the charter's allowed_paths enforcement. How to apply: future child-kind plans (governance_design in v2, etc.) should follow the same pattern — explicit authority declarations, no permissive defaults.

title: Return Condition is a structured ## section with status enum, not substring match
body: F002's child-charter close-out compliance does NOT use substring matching against the close-out memo. Instead, the close-out memo MUST contain a section whose heading is exactly `## Return Condition`, and within that section the FIRST line matching `^\s*status:\s*(satisfied|blocked|superseded)\s*$` (case-insensitive on keyword and value) determines the recorded `return_condition_status`. F003's parent re-entry approve refuses to clear `pre_resume_after_child` unless the child's signoff records `status: satisfied`. `blocked` and `superseded` are recorded but cannot resume the parent without an explicit `--accept-non-satisfied` operator override. Why: (a) substring matching is too loose — 'F002 EC5 finding resolved' and 'we tried but couldn't resolve the F002 EC5 finding' both contain the return_condition_summary text but mean opposite things; the structured status enum forces the operator to declare intent unambiguously; (b) the three legal statuses (satisfied, blocked, superseded) cover the realistic outcome space — 'satisfied' = parent return condition met; 'blocked' = child terminated without resolving (parent should rethink); 'superseded' = work moved to a different plan or scope changed (parent acceptance probably needs amendment); (c) the structured contract makes the close-out memo machine-readable in a narrow, durable way without requiring a schema bump on the memo itself. How to apply: any future close-out memo extension that needs machine validation should follow the same pattern — a designated `## Heading` section + a structured field — rather than freeform substring search.

title: F003 acceptance is hermetic synthetic; real dogfood is optional evidence
body: F003's acceptance proof is the hermetic synthetic e2e test under tmp_path with scripted executors. Real-dogfood trial (e.g., resurrecting the plan 005 F002 confirmation cycle as a recursive-finding test case) is welcomed as additional evidence if a clean recursive-finding case surfaces during implementation, but is NOT a hard acceptance criterion. The first implementation must not depend on resurrecting historically messy plans for validation. Why: (a) plan 005's F002 confirmation cycle is a specific historical sequence with audit-envelope shape that doesn't cleanly map to today's structured spawn metadata (D001) — adapting it would require fixture surgery that contaminates the test with plan-005-specific assumptions; (b) hermetic synthetic tests under tmp_path are easier to keep green over time as adjacent platform pieces evolve (signoff schema, gate-state shape, etc.); (c) real dogfood validates integration but should be an optional 'have we exercised this in anger?' evidence, not a 'this is the only way to know if it works' acceptance. The volley failure-taxonomy memory documents the trigger conditions for direct vs. volley dogfood; nested-orchestration's own dogfood readiness is a separate decision (operator-driven when a real recursive finding surfaces). How to apply: future platform-primitive plans should use this pattern — synthetic acceptance + optional real-dogfood evidence, NOT real-dogfood as the only proof.

title: events.jsonl is append-only best-effort trace, never canonical state
body: F003's `events.jsonl` writer is append-only and best-effort. `record_event(plan_dir, kind, payload)` wraps the file append in try/except (OSError, TypeError, json.JSONEncodeError); on failure it logs a WARNING with kind + plan_id + reason and returns silently. Event-write failures NEVER propagate or corrupt orchestration state. **Canonical state lives in plan files (plan.md, features.json), audit/gate-state.json, audit/<envelope>.json, and audit/signoff-*.json.** events.jsonl is a trace/index for human/operator visibility; missing events are an evidence-completeness issue, never a correctness issue. F003's acceptance includes a parametrized test that deletes events.jsonl on both parent and child mid-flow and verifies that the parent can still complete approve correctly because canonical state carries the load-bearing information. Why: (a) operational durability — disk-full / permission errors / concurrent-writer races on a trace file should never block orchestration progress; (b) clear separation of concerns — gate-state.json + signoff-*.json are the things that determine what the supervisor does next; events.jsonl is what helps a human reconstruct the timeline; conflating them invites correctness bugs ('we crashed because the trace log was wonky'); (c) future analytics layers reading events.jsonl should always be tolerant of gaps — if the analytics surface treats missing events as 'authoritative absence' rather than 'evidence incomplete,' it has a bug. How to apply: any future trace/index/observability surface (transcript.md, sentiment digests, metric exports) should follow the same best-effort discipline — write failures log + return, never raise. Canonical state stays in audit/* + plan files.

title: F001 close-out — direct path (no volley) for parent/child metadata + depth/cycle guards
body: F001 shipped via TDD red→green direct path — no volley dispatched. Operator-approved: schema/validation/guard slice with mostly deterministic tests, locked decisions (D001-D006), and minimal design ambiguity. A volley would be more useful once F003 parent-pause/fan-in surface exists to dogfood a real child flow; F001 alone is mechanical. Direct path delivered: nested_orchestration.py module (SpawnFinding + Orchestration Pydantic models, compute_finding_signature, walk_parent_chain, compute_depth, check_depth/cycle/repeated_finding, NestedOrchestrationError), plan_loader extended with `orchestration: Orchestration | None` field (frontmatter `orchestration` block popped BEFORE Plan.model_validate per D006-style schema discipline — agent-conventions/schemas unchanged), supervisor wires _run_nested_orch_guards into BOTH dispatch_single_agent (line ~480) AND dispatch_volley (line ~700), `--allow-depth N` CLI flag added (D002 — operator-only override; frontmatter cannot raise platform cap of 3), depth_override marker recorded in audit envelope's validation_performed for audit-trail visibility. Test/lint state at close-out: 21/21 F001 targeted tests pass, 490 + 6 skipped full orchestrate suite (was 469 → +21), ruff clean, sanitization clean (557 files). All six lock-time tightenings (D001-D006) implemented: structured spawn identity with SHA-256 finding_signature; CLI-only depth override; signature-based repeated-finding hard stop (not just code+class); plus Pydantic cross-field invariants for spawn_reason/spawn_finding consistency. F002 (child charter + commit policy) and F003 (parent pause/fan-in) NOT touched in this commit per scope discipline. Plan 003 ships F001 of 3 features; F002 next.

title: F002 — charter compliance recorded as side-car JSON, not embedded in signoff envelope (schema-discipline deviation from lock-time AC#6)
body: F002's `check_child_charter_compliance` returns a dict that signoff_writer persists to `audit/charter-compliance-{plan_id}.json` instead of embedding `return_condition_status` and `compliance_checks_satisfied` inside the signoff envelope. The lock-time acceptance text said 'signoff_data["return_condition_status"] = satisfied'; embedding requires a Signoff-schema bump (the model has `extra="forbid"`), which the F001 D006-style discipline pattern explicitly rejects (agent-conventions/schemas/v1.0 stays unchanged for nested-orchestration v1). The side-car path keeps the schema discipline AND surfaces the same artifact for F003 to read. Why this is the right deviation: (a) consistency — F001 already established 'parser-level concerns live outside agent-conventions schemas' (orchestration block popped before Plan.model_validate); (b) F003's `pre_resume_after_child` approve will read the child's side-car at `<child_plan_dir>/audit/charter-compliance-{child_plan_id}.json` — same logic as it would have read signoff_data[k]; (c) the side-car is co-located with the signoff envelope under audit/, so operators see both artifacts together and can correlate via filenames; (d) bumping the schema would require an agent-conventions VERSION bump + subtree pull + downstream consumers (Glam/SpinDine) to upgrade — disproportionate cost for a side-car-equivalent payload. How to apply: any future signoff-time enforcement check that records auxiliary state (compliance, lineage, evidence-graph metadata) should follow the same side-car pattern by default. Schema-bump only when the new field is canonical state that ANY consumer of agent-conventions Signoff might need (the bar is high).

title: F002 close-out — direct path (no volley) for child charter + commit policy + signoff-time compliance
body: F002 shipped via TDD red→green direct path. Operator-approved: bounded model/parsing/signoff-hook slice with deterministic tests, locked decisions (D003 + D004) covering the only design ambiguity (cross-field invariant + structured Return Condition section), and zero blast-radius outside nested-orchestration code paths. Volley still deferred until F003 dogfoods a real parent→child→close-out cycle. Direct path delivered: ChildCharter + CommitPolicy Pydantic models (D003 cross-field invariant in validate_charter_policy_consistency; governance_design + parent_squash rejected with deferral messages); ReturnConditionError + ChildCharterViolation exceptions; parse_return_condition_section (D004 — heading-anchored, status enum, case-insensitive keyword/value, rejects multiple status lines + h3 headings); check_child_charter_compliance (return-condition + allowed_paths under child_commit + requires items); plan_loader extended with optional child_charter/commit_policy fields + cross-validation (charter requires parent_plan_id, default policy synthesis, mode↔may_edit_product_code consistency); signoff_writer.write_signoff extended with optional charter/policy/modified_files kwargs + side-car write (D008); supervisor.dispatch_volley threads loaded.child_charter + loaded.commit_policy into write_signoff and catches ChildCharterViolation. Test/lint state at close-out: 51/51 F002 targeted tests pass, 541 + 6 skipped full orchestrate suite (was 490 → +51), ruff clean, sanitization clean (559 files). may_spawn_children grandchild dispatch-time refusal is intentionally deferred to F003 per operator's tight-boundary directive (the field is on the model with default=False; the runtime guard wires alongside parent-pause logic). Plan 003 status: F001 + F002 closed, F003 (parent pause/fan-in protocol) is next.

title: F003 — fan-in memo's own status must always be 'satisfied'; --accept-non-satisfied overrides only the child-side compliance status
body: approve_pre_resume_after_child enforces a two-layer status check (D004 contract + operator declaration). Layer 1: the operator-authored `evidence/fan-in-from-{child}.md` MUST contain `## Return Condition / status: satisfied`. The memo is the operator's explicit re-entry declaration; if they want to abandon parent re-entry the answer is 'do not author the memo at all', not 'declare blocked'. Layer 2: the child's `audit/charter-compliance-{child}.json` records the child's own outcome (satisfied | blocked | superseded — the F002 D004 enum). The `--accept-non-satisfied` CLI flag overrides ONLY layer 2 — letting the operator choose to resume parent despite a non-satisfied child outcome. Why this asymmetry: (a) the memo is FRESH operator intent at re-entry time; the side-car is HISTORICAL outcome from when the child finished. They serve different purposes — overriding the historical record without the fresh declaration would let an operator silently ignore a non-trivial finding by reusing a stale memo. (b) it forces the operator to acknowledge in writing 'I have reviewed and am proceeding' before bypassing the child status; the override flag becomes a tracked exception rather than a routine bypass. (c) the override is recorded in INBOX `gate_cleared` body with `OVERRIDE applied (--accept-non-satisfied)` line; the test suite parametrizes both clean and override paths. How to apply: any future operator-override pattern that bypasses an enforced status check should follow the same shape — fresh operator declaration (durable artifact) PLUS override flag, never override flag alone.

title: F003 close-out — direct path (no volley) for parent pause/fan-in protocol + stricter verification
body: F003 shipped via direct path with stricter verification per operator directive. Locked decisions D004 (structured Return Condition) and D006 (events.jsonl best-effort) covered the design ambiguity; remaining work was state-machine wiring + CLI handler + test coverage. Direct path delivered: pre_resume_after_child:{child_plan_id} as a third transient gate kind in gate_pause.py (alongside breakers + defers), with active_pre_resume_after_children stored separately so resume_all() does NOT touch it (bare-resume discipline); record_event in nested_orchestration.py (best-effort append-only JSON line; logs WARNING + returns False on OSError/JSONEncodeError; NEVER raises per D006); approve_pre_resume_after_child helper enforces gate-armed → memo-exists → memo-satisfied (D010, never overridden) → child-compliance-satisfied OR --accept-non-satisfied; CLI _approve_main routes `pre_resume_after_child` (no suffix) + --child to validating handler, refuses bare suffix form `pre_resume_after_child:CHILD` AND `resume --gate pre_resume_after_child:*`; supervisor _arm_parent_pre_resume_gate_for_child invoked after F001 guards in both dispatch paths (writes INBOX nested_child_pending once, idempotent; best-effort spawn_child trace on each dispatch); signoff_writer extended with optional orchestration kwarg → records best-effort volley.return_to_parent on child's events.jsonl when signoff lands. 38/38 F003 targeted tests pass with stricter verification: hermetic synthetic e2e (full lifecycle), canonical-state-primacy (events.jsonl deletion + monkeypatched record_event failure both leave approve working), bare-resume discipline (resume --gate refused, resume --all preserves), explicit-approve refusal of non-satisfied child without override + INBOX OVERRIDE entry on override path. Full orchestrate suite 579 + 6 skipped (was 541 → +38), ruff clean, sanitization clean (561 files). Plan 003 v1 closed: F001 + F002 + F003 all passing. governance assessment, ADR proposals, matrices, child-spawning automation, and may_spawn_children dispatch-time refusal explicitly deferred to v2 per scope discipline.

title: Nested-orchestration v2 is demand-driven — deferred until v1 has one real dogfood cycle
body: v2 (governance assessment, ADR proposals, geometry matrices, child-spawning automation, may_spawn_children dispatch-time grandchild refusal) does NOT get scheduled. It triggers on a real recursive finding, not on a calendar. **Trigger condition**: the first auditor finding that (a) requires child-plan work AND (b) is not solvable inside the parent plan's scope. When that finding surfaces in any future volley, the operator runs the v1 surface end-to-end against it (F001 dispatch with orchestration block → F002 child charter → F003 parent pause / fan-in memo / approve), captures concrete lessons during that real cycle, and only THEN drafts v2 from the evidence. Why demand-driven: (a) timed reminders create work detached from evidence — a v2 plan written before any real cycle would mostly speculate at shapes the real flow ends up not needing; (b) v1's anti-recursion thesis is structurally complete (depth + cycle + signature + charter + explicit-approval-with-status-satisfied), so the platform is safe to USE while we wait — the question is what governance/automation v2 surfaces are actually load-bearing, and that requires a real run; (c) the operator memory (`feedback_no_meta_systems_mid_volley.md`) already captures the principle that coordination primitives shouldn't be layered without finished real-world signal; v2 governance is exactly that kind of meta-system. How to apply: any future plan that says 'we should also build governance/observability/orchestration upgrades' should pass the same trigger test — what's the concrete failure mode in a real run that motivates this surface? If the answer is 'we haven't run it yet,' defer until you have. The v1 surface is the dogfood instrument; the next real recursive finding is the trigger; lessons from that single cycle become v2's evidence base.

title: v1 is the safe-nesting substrate, NOT the full governance layer — the governance layer is incomplete and the next increment is bootstrap-only
body: Correction to D012's framing: v1 (F001 + F002 + F003) shipped the safe-nesting SUBSTRATE — parent/child metadata, depth/cycle/repeated-finding guards, child charter, commit policy, parent pause / fan-in, return-condition enforcement, best-effort event trace. That set prevents recursion chaos. It does NOT solve higher-level delivery governance. The governance layer is a separate, incomplete concern. **Missing governance surfaces (operator inventory):** objective_contract; governance_assessment; project_maturity_detection; governing_doc_discovery; ADR_proposal_workflow; standards_gap_mechanism; stage_aware_geometry (linear/sidecar/fan_out/matrix patterns + per-stage caps); UX / product / release governance roles; parity governance (cross-platform invariant enforcement); cross-plan strategic alignment summaries. **Why the layer needs development:** v1 ensures a child plan is bounded and returns cleanly; it does NOT establish what the child should be doing relative to project standards, prior decisions, maturity stage, or strategic objectives. Without governance the substrate can run safely AND irrelevantly — bounded recursion of work that's misaligned with where the project actually is. **Why NOT build everything next:** v2 should be driven by the first real case where v1 is insufficient (D012 trigger) — AND when that case arrives the next plan should be a tight bootstrap, not the whole end-to-end operating model. **Candidate next plan: 'Nested Orchestration V2 — Governance Bootstrap'** with three features only: F001 = objective_contract + governing-docs inheritance; F002 = governance_assessment + standards_gap records; F003 = adr_proposal child kind + parent approval workflow. Stage-aware matrices, UX/product/release governance roles, and parity-specific enforcement explicitly defer to subsequent increments (not bundled into bootstrap). How to apply: when the trigger fires, the v2-bootstrap proposal goes through the normal lock cycle — operator-tightenings + locked decisions + scoped commits — same discipline as v1. Resist the pull to bundle 'while we're at it' surfaces; bootstrap is bootstrap. Subsequent increments name their own real-need trigger.
